messages:
ashley.nguyen: quick RFC follow-up — we need a concrete cutover playbook for handing query traffic from console-query v1 -> v2 (authz move from front-door to pushdown). low-risk incremental strategy please.

mike.kapoor: +1. main concerns: RBAC correctness during overlap, cache TTL/invalidations, and keeping dashboard P95s stable.

devin.lee: suggested steps: 1) feature flag gating per-tenant 2) canary 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback on SLO breach 3) keep v1 alive as fallback 4) gradual warmup of caches on v2.

ashley.nguyen: thanks. what about authorization semantics? pushdown means query nodes call authz service for row-level/column-level checks, right? how do we avoid N+1s on hot paths.

devin.lee: correct. tradeoffs: pushdown gives consistent enforcement and simpler UI-layer, but increases authz qps. mitigation: batch-check tokens for a batch of row ids, and use a local allowlist cache with short TTL (30s). also precompute simple allow masks for frequent dashboards.

tara: batch-check sounds good but we need to be explicit about stale-allow windows. dashboards often show near-real-time counts; a 30s cache might be visible. ops: add a metrics tag `authz_cache_staleness` so we can alert if it climbs.

mike.kapoor: for rollback we also need a fast circuit breaker so request routing can flip back to v1 without dropping sessions. can we re-route at the edge?

devin.lee: yes — routing policy will be a per-tenant flag in the routing service. pseudo-config: 
```yaml
routing_policy:
  tenant: tenant-id
  rollout_pct: 5
  fallback: v1
  authz_mode: pushdown
```
flip is atomic in control plane; edge picks it up within ~5s.

ashley.nguyen: ops checklist items: - pre-cutover load test with authz QPS doubled - telemetry dashboard (p95 latency, error-rate, authz_miss_rate) - cache invalidation playbook - canary tenants list - runbook for rollback 

mike.kapoor: cache invalidation playbook: run `authz-cachectl invalidate --tenant tenant-id --prefix dashboard-` or POST to /internal/evict. add audit log for invalidation events.

ashley.nguyen: noted. also need E2E tests to cover mixed state (some requests on v1, some on v2). integration test harness task assigned.

tara: question on quotas: if pushdown increases authz QPS we might blow org-level quota for some tenants. should we provide per-tenant throttle or billing compensation?

devin.lee: plan: soft-limit with token bucket per-tenant on authz service. on throttle, return `429` with header `X-Cutover-Disabled: true` so routing fallback triggers automatically. Also send SaaS billing event for increased authz usage.

ashley.nguyen: final decision summary: incremental per-tenant rollout via feature flags, pushdown authz with batched checks + short local cache, routing-level fallback & circuit breaker, explicit invalidation CLI + internal endpoint, telemetry & SLO gates for automatic rollback.

mike.kapoor: will draft the playbook doc and the ops checklist. tagging infra for the routing flag propagation test.

sre-bot: deploybot: created deploy request #5483 for canary infra changes (routing flag + metrics).

ashley.nguyen: thanks. @devin.lee @mike.kapoor @tara please ack when you have action items added to your boards. :thumbsup:

mike.kapoor: ack :thumbsup:

devin.lee: ack :thumbsup:

tara: ack :thumbsup:
